idiom_name: value-returning functions over const inputs; C23 [[reproducible]] / [[unsequenced]] function attributes
implementation_notes: C has no purity checking, so the discipline is expressed by what the function touches: take inputs as values or pointers to const data, return a result by value, and write through no other pointer. GCC and Clang accept __attribute__((pure)) (no side effects, may read globals) and __attribute__((const)) (result depends only on the arguments) so the optimiser can reuse or eliminate repeated calls; C23 standardised the same promises as [[reproducible]] (effectless and idempotent) and [[unsequenced]] (effectless, idempotent, stateless and independent) on the function type. Nothing in the language enforces either form, so keep mutations in small void-returning command functions and treat every attribute as a promise the compiler records but cannot check.
pitfalls: const is shallow and advisory: const Money *m still lets the data behind the pointer be changed elsewhere, and a cast can drop const qualifiers entirely.

A pure/const/[[reproducible]]/[[unsequenced]] annotation is an unchecked promise: if the function observes a global or thread-local that changes between calls (a clock, errno, a config flag), the compiler may reuse a stale result.
Out-parameters and non-reentrant library calls (static buffers, strtok-style APIs) reintroduce hidden state even when no global is written explicitly.
